activities.caption: drag the divider — ownership vs loan
activities.name: sbClaimsCompare

config.prompt: The two claims everything is built from — drag the divider:

before.label: Stock — ownership
before.text: A residual claim: profits arrive as dividends or retained growth, a vote elects the board, and liquidation pays you last. Upside unbounded; in bad outcomes shareholders absorb losses until wiped out.

after.label: Bond — a loan
after.text: Fixed coupons plus principal at maturity. Upside capped at the schedule; priority in trouble sits near the front of the queue.

config.why: Understanding what you actually hold — a share of profits or a loan contract — explains both the returns and the risks of everything built on top.

activities.anchor: That position explains the return profile
activities.caption: pair each right with what it buys you
activities.name: sbRightsMatch

config.prompt: What a share of common stock attaches — pair each right with its meaning:

pairs.right: paid as dividends or retained for growth
paid after employees, suppliers, lenders and bondholders
the worst case capped at your investment — failure cannot follow you home
the company sells shares to the public and gets the money

config.why: Afterwards the shares trade on secondary markets — NYSE, Nasdaq, LSE — where the company receives nothing and prices are the market's running vote on the discounted value of all future profits.

config.prompt: The ratings ladder: where does the investment-grade floor sit?
config.why: AAA to BBB− is investment grade — most regulated funds may hold it; below that is high yield, junk, where the credit analysis of leverage, coverage and collateral has found real doubt.

activities.anchor: Sensitivity to rates is summarised by
activities.caption: call the swing — duration at 30 years
activities.name: sbDurationEstimate

config.prompt: Rates rise 1 percentage point. Roughly how much price does a 30-year bond lose?
config.why: About 17–19 per cent (a 10-year bond loses roughly 7–8) — exactly what 2022 demonstrated: aggressive rate rises produced the worst global bond year on record, with major aggregate indices down around 13–16 per cent.

activities.anchor: a dividend strategy is a preference
activities.caption: bet before the ex-date
activities.name: sbExDivPredict

config.q: A company pays a 4 dividend. On the ex-dividend date, what does the share price do?
choices: Falls by roughly 4 — cash moved from the company's account to yours
config.why: The company has moved cash from its account to yours: what compounds is the whole return — the payout is an income choice, not an arbitrage.

activities.anchor: a bond held to maturity is risk-free
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the fixed-payments promise
activities.name: sbMaturitySpot

config.prompt: One line of this bond-holder's note is wrong — click it:
lines: The coupons and principal of a held bond are fixed.
The price of the bond is not.
The 1,000 bond fell to about 926 when rates rose one point.
A 30-year bond falls roughly five times harder than the 10-year.
Sell early and you keep the price you bought at.
config.correction: Sell early and the market re-prices you first — the fixed payments protect the cash flows, never the price.
config.why: The payments are fixed; the price is not — duration decides how hard the re-pricing bites, and whoever sells wears it.

activities.anchor: The analyst's core questions are about solvency under stress
activities.caption: grade the bond yourself
activities.name: sbGradeBranch

config.root: A corporate issuer is on your desk. The rating letter depends on your answers.

start.text: Debt stands at how many times annual operating profit?

choices.label: Three times
choices.feedback: Rideable — a company owing three times operating profit can usually absorb a bad year.

choices.label: Eight times
choices.feedback: Danger territory — one owing eight times may not.

coverage.text: Interest coverage: operating profit divided by the interest bill?

choices.label: Below 2 times
choices.feedback: The dividend of error is near zero.

grade.text: The letters compress your answers. Below BBB−, what changes mechanically?

choices.label: Index-tracking holders are forced to sell — the fallen-angel dynamic
choices.feedback: The downgrade itself pushes prices down further — the grade matters mechanically, not just descriptively.

choices.label: Nothing — the letters are descriptive only
choices.feedback: Regulated funds and index trackers are constrained by the grade — the selling is mechanical.

end.text: The reward for bearing the risk is the spread — in normal times 3–4 points over Treasuries; in panics it can blow out past 10, precisely when default risk (and opportunity) peaks.

config.why: Leverage, coverage and liquidity compress into letters — and reading spreads is reading the market's live estimate of how much trouble the economy is in.

activities.anchor: standing buy orders (bids) and sell orders (asks) ranked by price
activities.caption: true or false — the plumbing of a trade
activities.name: sbBookJudge

statements.s: The best bid and best ask bracket the spread.
statements.why: Market makers earn it for standing ready to trade — that is what liquidity means.

statements.s: In crises, spreads widen exactly when you most need to exit.
statements.why: The same share can be effortless to trade one week and gappy the next — liquidity is the invisible variable.

statements.s: Adding a stock to a major index changes its liquidity and often its price.
statements.why: Inclusion forces passive funds to buy it — index construction moves markets.

statements.s: Market orders are the right choice when size is large.
statements.why: Prefer limit orders when size is large — the spread is small, but it is being paid by someone.
